primary_work.title: Beyond identifiability: Learning causal representations with few environments and finite samples

decision: NARROWED BEYOND FINITE-SAMPLE UNKNOWN MULTI-TARGET CRL — NOT ADOPTED
prior_art_boundary: finite-sample consistent recovery of latent graph, decoder, representations, and unknown multi-node intervention targets is possible in the stated linear setting without language
logarithmically many strongly separating environments suffice under the paper assumptions
finite-sample target recovery does not identify raw-utterance equivalence or semantic denotation
label permutation remaining in the theorem is a residual semantic ambiguity unless externally anchored
counterexample: Two models related by simultaneous permutation of latent coordinates, decoder columns, graph labels, intervention-target sets, raw-utterance classes, denotation, and language encoder preserve every environment-indexed data law, covariance-subspace statistic, finite-sample estimator output, task metric, and language-conditioned prediction while assigning different semantic utterance-target correspondences.
official_code_status: primary paper and constructive algorithm verified; paper-specific official implementation not verified
